sections.title: Question & scope
sections.text: How do researched pediatric therapy providers in Austin and San Antonio differ in services and geographic footprints, and what should an analyst investigate next? This snapshot includes 19 unique companies across 20 company–market records. Geography: physical clinic presence. Required services: any core therapy. Dataset updated 2026-11-06 (UTC).

sections.title: Austin: the researched sample
sections.text: Among the 10 selected companies researched in Austin, 11 physical locations are documented. 9 records match the current screen and 1 remain uncertain. Branch-level evidence documents speech at 9 companies, occupational therapy at 8, and physical therapy at 5. These service groups overlap.

sections.title: San Antonio: the researched sample
sections.text: Among the 10 selected companies researched in San Antonio, 10 physical locations are documented. 8 records match the current screen and 2 remain uncertain. Branch-level evidence documents speech at 7 companies, occupational therapy at 7, and physical therapy at 6. These service groups overlap.

sections.title: What the differences tell us
sections.text: Austin and San Antonio have 10 and 10 selected companies, respectively. Differences in documented service mix may reflect both the sampled providers and the completeness of their websites. A clinic offering multiple services could be a useful operational comparator for the illustrative multiservice model.

sections.title: 1. Resolve clinic-level evidence
sections.text: Confirm which therapies operate at each branch, current addresses, and any conflicting age or service descriptions. Obtain a dated clinic service roster before treating uncertain records as matches.

sections.title: 2. Test access and referral assumptions
sections.text: Investigate waitlists, referral sources, pediatric population needs, and payer participation using dated interviews and published participation lists.

sections.title: 3. Build the operating case
sections.text: Research therapist availability, compensation, occupancy costs, reimbursement, and site economics. Compare these independently of the provider counts before considering an expansion decision.
